cards.explanation: The answer is the Most Holy Place. The writer says believers have “…confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus…” (Hebrews 10:19). Confidence is the key word, friends. He doesn't say "sneak in" or "tiptoe in." He says walk in like you were invited.
The answer is by the blood of Jesus. The writer says the confidence comes “…by the blood of Jesus…” (Hebrews 10:19). Nothing is added to it, friends. Nobody has to bring a résumé to the door.

The answer is True. The writer says it's “…the new and living way opened for us through the curtain of His body…” (Hebrews 10:20). The way is new, it's living, and it's already opened for us. Nobody has to go find a crowbar.
The answer is priest. The writer says “…we have a great priest over the house of God…” (Hebrews 10:21). He uses "great" on purpose, friends. That's a big title, and he doesn't mumble it.

The answer is "Let us draw near." After the open way and the great priest, the writer says, “…let us draw near…” (Hebrews 10:22). Notice it's "us," friends. He's walking up with them, not pointing from the back of the room.

The answer is a guilty conscience. The writer says their hearts are sprinkled “…to cleanse us from a guilty conscience…” (Hebrews 10:22). That's the cleaning job, friends. And it's done on the inside, where it's hardest to scrub.
The answer is True. The writer says, “…our bodies washed with pure water.” (Hebrews 10:22). So it's two things together: hearts sprinkled and bodies washed. Clean inside and clean outside.

The answer is that He who promised is faithful. The writer says, “…for He who promised is faithful.” (Hebrews 10:23). The grip is tight because of who made the promise, friends. The hope doesn't hang on how strong the one holding it feels today.

The answer is love and good deeds. The writer says, “And let us consider how to spur one another on to love and good deeds.” (Hebrews 10:24). So the spurring points somewhere good, friends. And you'll notice he says "one another," so everybody gets a turn.

The answer is neglecting meeting together. The writer says, “Let us not neglect meeting together, as some have made a habit…” (Hebrews 10:25). Some had made neglecting it a habit. Instead he says, “…but let us encourage one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.” (Hebrews 10:25).

The answer is False. The writer says, “…but let us encourage one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.” (Hebrews 10:25). All the more, friends! That's the same reason my ovens stay ready. I'm not guessing when the Day is, and the writer doesn't either.

The answer is a further sacrifice for sins. The writer says that if we deliberately go on sinning after receiving the knowledge of the truth, “…no further sacrifice for sins remains…” (Hebrews 10:26). It's a serious verse, friends. I think it's meant to make us take it seriously.

The answer is True. The writer says what's left is “…only a fearful expectation of judgment and of raging fire that will consume all adversaries.” (Hebrews 10:27). It's strong language, friends. I think he wants it to land.

The answer is that they died without mercy. The writer says, “Anyone who rejected the law of Moses died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.” (Hebrews 10:28). I think this one hurts, friends. It's here so the next verse can ask its question.

The answer is blood. The writer says this person “…has trampled on the Son of God, profaned the blood of the covenant that sanctified him, and insulted the Spirit of grace?” (Hebrews 10:29). Notice the Son, the blood of the covenant and the Spirit of grace all show up in that one verse. It's serious business, friends.

The answer is a fearful thing. The writer says, “It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.” (Hebrews 10:31). He doesn't soften it, friends. I think that's the point of the whole stop.

The answer is a great conflict in the face of suffering. The writer says, “…you endured a great conflict in the face of suffering.” (Hebrews 10:32). These folks had been through it, friends. And he reminds them they came through it.

The answer is False. The writer says, “Sometimes you were publicly exposed to ridicule and persecution; at other times you were partners with those who were so treated.” (Hebrews 10:33). So it happened to them, and they also stood beside others it happened to. That's a lot of loyalty, friends.

The answer is joyfully! The writer says they “…joyfully accepted the confiscation of your property…” (Hebrews 10:34). That's a hard thing to lose, friends, and they met it with joy. The same verse says they were “…knowing that you yourselves had a better and permanent possession.”

The answer is that they had a better and permanent possession. The writer says they accepted it joyfully, “…knowing that you yourselves had a better and permanent possession.” (Hebrews 10:34). The knowing is what carried them, friends. They held something that couldn't be taken.
The answer is a great reward. The writer says, “So do not throw away your confidence; it holds a great reward.” (Hebrews 10:35). Don't toss it, friends. There's something good inside.

The answer is persevere. The writer says, “You need to persevere, so that after you have done the will of God, you will receive what He has promised.” (Hebrews 10:36). Perseverance means sticking with it, friends. Like pressing out the last cookie of a huge batch when your arm is tired.
The answer is by faith. The quote says, “But My righteous one will live by faith…” (Hebrews 10:38). Faith is the word it gives for how the righteous one lives. Plain and simple, friends.
The answer is True. The quote says, “and if he shrinks back, I will take no pleasure in him.” (Hebrews 10:38). It's a sober line, friends. I think it's here to help us hold on.

The answer is those who have faith and preserve their souls. The writer says, “But we are not of those who shrink back and are destroyed, but of those who have faith and preserve their souls.” (Hebrews 10:39). Notice the "we," friends. He puts himself in the same group as his readers.
